limitations: Exchange market price can trade at a material premium or discount to NAV.
NAV uses a blended proprietary uranium spot-price benchmark, so benchmark/data rights must be reviewed before persistent automated ingestion.
This proxy starts in 2021 and cannot provide pre-inception uranium context.
Represents equity-market pricing of uranium/nuclear companies, not the uranium spot price.
Contains company, equity-beta, FX, financing and nuclear-industry effects beyond uranium itself.
Must remain a separate feature from the physical-uranium proxy and may not be spliced into it.

proxies.instrument: Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF
limitations: Represents the lithium/battery equity value chain, not a pure lithium commodity price.
Battery manufacturers and downstream companies can react differently from lithium producers when lithium prices move.
Equity beta, FX, technology sentiment and company-specific effects remain embedded.

proxies.instrument: CME Lithium Hydroxide / Lithium Carbonate CIF CJK Futures
limitations: Requires an explicit contract-selection and roll methodology; continuous back-adjusted histories may not be retrojected without provenance.
The underlying Fastmarkets benchmark and CME market data have separate usage/licensing conditions that must be cleared.
Liquidity varies materially by contract and date.

interpretation.uranium: Use SPUT NAV as the more commodity-like challenger from 2021 onward and URA as a separate longer-history equity-sector proxy from 2010 onward. Never splice them into one synthetic series.
interpretation.lithium: Prefer exchange-traded lithium futures as the commodity-like challenger if rights and liquidity gates pass; use LIT only as a separate long-history lithium/battery equity proxy.
